external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and fetches assets.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: A person who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
external_entities.notes: The admin connects from wherever they happen to be and there is no jump host.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: A content delivery network from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads and to which new assets are pushed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The web server serves the public site, runs the CMS, and participates in publishing assets to the CDN.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The content management system run by the web server.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: A database containing pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network
data_stores.notes: The source says it could not tell whether the database is encrypted on disk.

data_stores.name: bucket
data_stores.description: The CDN bucket receiving newly published assets.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket

data_flows.name: hit web server
data_flows.description: Readers access the public site through the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: Readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: keep content
data_flows.description: The CMS keeps pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: Nothing in the source tells how this push is authenticated.

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin maintains the database directly over an unsecured MySQL connection.
data_flows.source_excerpt: That is an unsecured MySQL connection straight to the box, no TLS on it
data_flows.notes: The admin connects from wherever they happen to be; there is no jump host.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server and MySQL database.

trust_boundaries.name: CDN
trust_boundaries.description: The trust zone associated with the externally operated CDN and its bucket.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet because it serves the public site to readers.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it the public site and says readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The CMS is located in the hosted network because the web server runs it and the web server is stated to be on that network.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web server runs the CMS and places the web server on the same hosted network as the database.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN is controlled outside the system's control, so it forms a tenant trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a CDN and its bucket as a separate service from which readers fetch assets and to which the web server pushes assets.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN entity is in the CDN tenant boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the external service as the CDN.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket is in the CDN tenant boundary because it is described as the CDN's bucket.
assumptions.basis: The source says the web server pushes assets to the CDN's bucket.
